notes: CIRCUIT: a six-op-amp active network. Two source ports (+15 V at top left, +10 V at mid left) drive two input stages (A1 = #3, A2 = #19); their outputs feed a summing stage A3 = #5 through 1k resistors; A3's output bus (the x~575 vertical) fans out to three parallel output stages A4 = #4 (1k in, 1uH feedback), A5 = #14 (1k in, 1uF feedback) and A6 = #25 (1uF in, 1uH feedback); the three stage outputs each pass through a 1k resistor to a common vertical bus at x~985 on the right edge. NET MAP (final labels from finalize.py): n1 = the +15 V rail y~322 x 55..286 - port #0, A1's in- (via the x~119 drop at S1), A1's OUTPUT (the wire drops at x~286 into the output apex at S23) and the left end of R7. n2 = A3's in+ node - right end of R7, the x~423 stub up to the left end of L1 (S25). n3 = A3's OUTPUT bus - the x~575 vertical from y~310 down to y~680: right end of L1, A3's apex (S28), left end of R6 (S24), left end of R16 (S57), left plate of C23. n4 = A4's in- node - right end of R6, left end of L2 (S22). n5 = A4's OUTPUT - apex, right end of L2 (S26), left end of R8. n6 = A3's in- node - the x~419 column: right end of R11 (S37), top of the vertical 1k R15 (whose bottom goes to GND #21). n7 = the right-hand output bus x~985 y 390..700: right ends of R8, R17 and R26. n8 = A2's OUTPUT node - apex, right end of L18 (S62), left end of R11. n9 = A5's OUTPUT - apex (S60), right plate of C12, left end of R17. n10 = A5's in- node - left plate of C12, right end of R16, A5's upper-left input lead. n11 = the +10 V node - port #13, the y~548 wire, left end of L18, A2's in- (via the x~130 drop at S61). n12 = A6's in- node - right plate of C23, left end of L22. n13 = A6's OUTPUT - apex (S86), right end of L22, left end of R26. 0 = the six GND symbols (#9,#10,#20,#21,#24,#27) plus the in+ pin of A1, A2, A4, A5, A6 and the bottom of R15. JUDGEMENT CALLS: none of the 13 CRITICAL sites is an ambiguous crossing - every one is a plain T where one wire ends on another, and I recorded 'junction' for each after looking at its crop: S1 (119,322) +15 V rail branching down to A1's in-; S22 (675,370) R6's right end meeting the L2 stub; S23 (286,372) the +15 V feedback wire landing on A1's output; S24 (574,372) R6's left lead landing on A3's output bus; S25 (423,382) R7's right end meeting the L1 stub; S26 (826,385) A4's apex meeting the L2 return; S28 (575,397) A3's apex meeting its output bus; S37 (419,472) R11's right end meeting the A3 in- column; S57 (577,528) R16's left end on the output bus; S60 (812,542) A5's apex meeting the C12 return; S61 (130,545) the +10 V wire branching down to A2's in-; S62 (306,551) L18's right-hand wire ending on the A2-output/R11 line - this is the A2 feedback connection, and reading it as a crossing would leave L18's right end dangling and split A2's output from R11; S86 (822,696) A6's apex meeting the L22 return. There are no hops or solder dots anywhere on this sheet. PIN-ORDER / PORT FIXES (Op-Amp order is in+, in-, out): the drafter marks + and - inside the triangle. A1 #3, A2 #19: '-' upper-left, '+' lower-left -> t0=lower-left port, t1=upper-left port, t2=apex. A3 #5 is drawn with the marks REVERSED - '+' is the upper-left input and '-' the lower-left (verified at 5x) - so t0 = p2 (443,380), t1 = p1 (442,431), t2 = p0 (550,396); the tracer had the apex as t0. A4 #4: the tracer had never mapped the in+ lead at all (t1 pointed at p2, a stroke of the '1uH' label sitting above the box, which produced the one-terminal net n6); the real in+ is p4 (701,414), which runs to GND #10. A5 #14: same failure - t1 pointed at p2 (767,596), a '1uH' label stroke below the box (one-terminal net n13); the real in+ is p5 (688,561), which runs to GND #20. A6 #25: t0/t2 swapped, apex is the output. V-DC #13 (+10 V): the tracer used p0 (56,468), the tip of the arrowhead, which is a dead end (one-terminal net n12); the real terminal is p1 (51,510), the stem that runs down to y~545 and then right into the A2 input wire. Resistor #17: t1 pointed at p1 (942,522), a stroke of the handwritten '1k Ohm'; the real right lead is p3 (941,543). MERGES (both explained, both are pen-lifts, not design gaps): (a) ['16.1','12.1'] - R16's right lead. The tracer found no port on the right side of R16's box, so t1 fell onto p2 (619,507), a label stroke, giving the one-terminal net n14. The inkmap at (660,522) shows the resistor's right lead running unbroken from x~646 to x~686 at y~525 and meeting the x~658 vertical that climbs to the C12 feedback wire, so R16's right terminal is electrically the A5 in- node; merging it with C12's left plate (12.1) puts it on exactly that node (n10) and nothing else, because n14 contained no other terminal. (b) ['17.1','8.1'] - R17's right lead ends at x=977,y=541 and the right-hand bus is at x=983..986; the inkmap at (968,546) shows a 5-pixel paper gap against a 3-4 pixel stroke, with the lead aimed straight at the bus. The other two output resistors (R8 above, R26 below) land on the same bus solidly, so this is a pen lift and the drafter plainly meant contact. Without the merge, R17's right terminal is a one-terminal net. NOTED, NOT ERRORS: (i) A1 (#3) has its in- shorted to its output AND to the +15 V port - that is what is drawn (the y~322 wire runs unbroken from the +15 V stem at x~55 to x~286 and then down onto the output apex, with a branch at x~119 down to the in- lead). It makes A1 a buffer whose summing node is driven hard by the source; I checked the crop at 5x and there is no break and no series element in that wire. (ii) A3 (#5) is drawn with its 1uH feedback returning to the '+' input, i.e. positive feedback, and with the 1k/1k divider on the '-' input; unusual, but the + and - marks are legible and unambiguous. (iii) n7, the right-hand bus, touches only three resistor right-ends and nothing else - it is the network's output/summing node and the drafter drew nothing beyond it. (iv) Capacitor #12's t1 sits on port p1 (736,500), which is a stroke of the '1uF' label rather than the plate lead; the tracer found no left-side port. The label stroke is fused to the feedback wire (1 px gap, bridged), so the resulting net n10 is the electrically correct one - the cap's left plate does connect to the A5 in- node via the x~669 drop - and I left it. All other 'unused port candidate' warnings are handwritten value labels ('1k Ohm', '1uH', '1uF', '+10V') brushing the boxes.
